title: Kalani
description: Kalani. A Farmer's Assistant. An English and Tamil farmer assistant. Current iPhone prototype; Android and web clients planned. A concrete farmer problem mapped to an evaluator-ready user journey.

slides.imageCaption: Actual iPhone Simulator capture · English evaluation demo
slides.notes: Kalani is a farmer-assistant product intended for iOS, Android and web. The current implemented client and today's demonstration run on iPhone Simulator. Android and web clients remain planned. I will show the farmer journey in English, then the Tamil language switch. The shared backend connects a concern to confirmed farm context, evidence and farmer-controlled decisions. The goal is useful next-step guidance, not a claimed improvement in farm outcomes.

slides.focus: What should I do this week?
slides.footnote: Regional Indian studies support local, understandable advisory information. The scenario is illustrative.
slides.notes: The concrete problem is translating information into a decision for this field. A 2017 study in four NCR Delhi villages found farmers valued understandable advisories with familiar words and local applicability. A 2018 Almora study identified weather, farm advice and market information as important ICT uses. These regional findings support the information need. Our inference is that a concern-led, contextual conversation can help connect those pieces. The rain question is an illustrative scenario, not a completed Kalani farmer interview or an impact result.

slides.focusTranslation: Observe clarity, completion and farmer control.
slides.footnote: Missing facts trigger a question. Tasks require current evidence. The farmer keeps the final choice.
slides.notes: Follow one concern through the visible app screens. Begin in English. In Conversation, ask whether rain affects this week's work by voice or text. Confirm crop and village in My Farm, including a known weather location when needed. In Today, inspect the reply, date, source and replay control. Ask a follow-up if the answer is unclear. This Week supports a separate decision when valid evidence produces a task. Return later to correct facts or report work. The observer should record confusion, assistance and recovery, rather than assume successful use.

slides.notes: These two captures show the same My Farm screen in English and Tamil, with the language selector visible. English is selected for the invigilator's demonstration. Switching to Tamil changes the app labels, and the saved preference controls the language of future conversations and speech. Existing messages keep their original language. Today, Conversation, This Week and My Farm keep the same navigation structure in either language.

slides.notes: The current iPhone client talks to one TypeScript backend. Android and web are future clients for the same product journey, not completed builds. Pi Durable coordinates checkpointed work and uses Claude through its Anthropic provider. Relevant specialists contribute bounded findings, which are reconciled and validated before publication. SQLite holds authoritative state. Speech adapters support the selected English or Tamil locale. Future clients can reuse backend capabilities while their own interfaces and usability still need implementation and review.

slides.footnote: Diagram combines two existing synthetic tests. No live farm advice or measured outcome.
slides.notes: This diagram combines two existing synthetic tests. In the unchanged-context test, repeated submission produces one workflow and one proposed task. In the correction test, the crop changes from rice to cotton at the publication checkpoint. The old request is superseded and publishes neither a reply nor a task. This is engineering evidence about consistency, not an agricultural recommendation or a completed field demonstration.

slides.title: Usability checks tied to the farmer's goal
slides.subtitle: Observe whether the person can navigate, understand the evidence and control the next step.
slides.footnote: Observe independent navigation, clarity and recoverable mistakes. Task actions depend on valid guidance.
slides.notes: This is the invigilator's checklist, not a claim of completed farmer testing. First, switch English to Tamil and back, then reopen the demo and verify English persists. Second, find voice or text input and check preview, consent and retry. Third, find a reply's source, date and uncertainty, and explain its meaning. Fourth, correct a farm fact and distinguish agreeing to a proposed task from reporting completion. Task decisions can be demonstrated only when supported guidance has produced a task. Record where help is needed and whether mistakes can be corrected.

slides.footnote: 18 Nov 2026: 52 passed in the full run; the sandbox-blocked HTTP test passed separately with loopback access.
slides.notes: The current TypeScript compilation passed. Fifty-two backend tests passed in the full run. The HTTP test was blocked by sandbox socket permissions, then passed separately with loopback access, giving passing results for all fifty-three. A language-switch regression checks that an in-flight English recording keeps its English reply even if the farmer switches to Tamil. Tests use synthetic providers and do not establish speech quality, agricultural accuracy or production readiness.

slides.title: iOS, Android and web
slides.subtitle: One product across three platforms. Today's demonstration runs on iPhone.
slides.footnote: Android/web clients, reviewed crop/scheme coverage, field validation and production delivery remain ahead.
slides.notes: Kalani's product direction covers iOS, Android and web. The implemented client today is the iPhone Simulator app, connected to the local backend. Android and farmer-facing web clients are planned, with the same intended conversations, evidence and farmer-controlled decisions. Their client interfaces and usability still need to be built and verified. The public link shared with this pitch hosts the presentation. Reviewed source coverage, field validation, production hosting and delivery remain future gates. No adoption, profit or yield impact is established.

slides.focus: Can the farmer explain the next step?
slides.footnote: Kalani · A Farmer's Assistant · Local prototype · 18 November 2026
slides.notes: I am looking for agricultural review of evidence and local applicability, English and Tamil review of comprehension and usability, and engineering review of reliability and future Android and web clients. The invigilator can start in English, inspect the two language states and follow the concern-to-decision map. The immediate question is whether a farmer can understand and explain a supported next step while retaining control. That needs structured user review before a field pilot or impact claim.
